Subject: Draft DPA + SCCs questions before legal review

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal team has taken a first pass at the DPA you sent and flagged a few items we want to align on before we send redlines back to procurement. High-level:

- We need a short mapping of where the DPA obligations live vs the MSA/order form (processors, subprocessors, data flows).
- Clarify whether Redwood's private deployment option is a permitted hosting fallback (we have a security point here).
- Confirm what version of the SCCs you're relying on and whether you accept the standard EU addendum we usually attach.

I've copied Jacob from procurement — he will coordinate timing for signature. Can you point us to the latest MSA + order form mapping and a contact on the technical side for hosting residency questions?

Thanks,
Sophie

Head of Legal, Healthline Systems

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-10-29T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft DPA + SCCs questions before legal review

Hi Sophie — thanks, and good questions. Quick answers and a proposed execution approach below.

1) Mapping: attaching an MSA->Order Form->DPA mapping workbook that ties each DPA clause to the MSA and the order form line items (who is controller/processor, subprocessor callouts). That should make it straightforward for your counsel to see where obligations flow.

2) Private deployment fallback: Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) is an available option but is subject to an addendum for network and KMS controls. For contract impact we usually surface that as a hosting "fallback" clause with a pricing/breach trigger. Laura (cc) can outline the standard addendum language and exceptions.

3) SCCs: We onboard on the 2021 SCCs as baseline and attach our annotated SCCs_Matrix for transparency. If Healthline prefers a customer-provided SCC addendum, we can accept with limited carveouts around subprocessors (we'll document those).

Proposed next steps (execution sprint):
- Today (T+0): I attach the MSA_OrderForm_Mapping.xlsx and SCCs_Matrix_annotated.pdf for your review.
- T+2 (48 hrs): Sophie/legal provide targeted redlines to DPA (or confirm matrix agreement).
- T+5: Redwood legal turn on internal review + produce clean redlines for DocuSign.
- T+7: Signatures and handback to procurement for billing activation.

We can accelerate if you want a short call with Laura and our security engineer; happy to set up a 30-min slot.

Attachments: MSA_OrderForm_Mapping.xlsx (xlsx), SCCs_Matrix_annotated.pdf (pdf)

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: DPA + SCCs: execution sprint & legal liaison plan

Sophie — attaching our initial redlines for the DPA. Key changes we propose:

- Clause 4 (Subprocessor onboarding): add 14-day notice window and customer approval right for any subprocessor with access to unredacted customer data.
- Clause 7 (Cross-border transfers): reference the SCCs matrix and add a commitment to provide export-log evidence upon reasonable request.
- Clause 11 (Security measures): add the VPC/KMS chart as an exhibit (we'll link to the hosting addendum if customer chooses Private).

I've put comments in the Word doc where we expect the most back-and-forth; redlines are conservative to keep negotiation runway. Laura — please confirm whether the subprocessor approval language is acceptable for enterprise deals or if we should reduce the notice to 7 days.

Attachments: Healthline_DPA_Redlines_v1.docx (docx)

—Ben
